title: Daily AI papers — arXiv announcement batch 2026-11-11
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; ordering is inferred from sparse corroborating signals. All seven selected papers had zero Semantic Scholar citations and zero influential citations at the 2026-11-13 01:10:10 UTC snapshot, so this is a notable-recent-papers shortlist, not a measured popularity ranking.

sections.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
sections.abstract: ReTrace converts an SOP and a few logged agent runs into reusable executable workflows that choose steps without an LLM planner, reporting near-agent task completion with lower cost and much lower latency in tested settings.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors extract action conditions from agent reasoning and tool traces, merge them into an evidence-linked rule document, then compile platform-specific workflows; their tests report 93.8% completion on 79 production procedures at 24% lower task cost, and 1.3 s versus 170 s per task on τ²-bench.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say generated-workflow checks do not establish that recovered conditions are correct; evaluation covers new inputs to the same procedures, not transfer to new procedures, and platform completion flags can misreport failures.

sections.title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
sections.abstract: Pyrite introduces a 1,500-pair protein–ligand pose-ranking benchmark and structured molecular features for LLM agents, reporting up to 74% accuracy for an LLM-guided feature-engineering pipeline.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce PyriteRep and compare direct LLM pose reasoning with LLM-generated features for logistic regression; the latter reaches 74% on their benchmark, while expert chemists perform near chance on the evaluated pairs.
sections.unique_caveat: The benchmark poses come from the authors’ proprietary cofolding model; they flag possible pre-/post-AF3 distribution shift and leave transfer to other pose generators and downstream drug-discovery pipelines for future work.

sections.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
sections.abstract: Contrastive Discovery makes an agent evaluate a scientific question against explicit competing explanations rather than a single claim and its negation, reporting more resolved questions under matched evidence and experiment budgets.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across six data-driven domains, authors report 67% more resolved questions than pointwise surprisal under the same experiment budget; a blinded study of 38 experts agreed with the selected explanation on 78% of resolved questions.
sections.unique_caveat: The study uses observational tabular datasets and one GPT-4o-based agent; the authors note that conclusions are statistical rather than causal and that results remain to be tested in laboratory experiments and longer-horizon interventions.

sections.title: When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents
sections.abstract: FGSE treats a proposed agent-memory update as a hypothesis, probes transfer, falsification, and regression risks in temporary state, and commits, revises, or rejects it using verifier-grounded evidence.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 39.8 WebArena success, 78.8 AppWorld average completion, and reductions in falsification failures, regression damage, and harmful committed updates using their commit–refine–reject process.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evidence is from verifier-rich benchmarks; the authors leave extension to multimodal or collaborative agents and settings where verifiers must be learned or approximated to future work.

sections.title: Multimodal Abstention That Preserves Acquired Correct Answers
sections.abstract: ReFrain adds calibrated abstention to a task-adapted vision-language model while constraining newly lost correct answers, reporting improved refusal of unanswerable image questions with fewer regressions than compared methods.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author combines a first-token-logit probe, held-out image-cluster threshold calibration, and a deterministic veto; on Qwen2.5-VL-3B, the paper reports higher correct abstention at a specified calibration budget while retaining more SFT-gained answers than the comparison method.
sections.unique_caveat: The author reports a single training seed and a 677-record training set; independent confirmation covers AI2D science diagrams, and possible exposure of public AI2D data during model pretraining cannot be excluded.

sections.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
sections.abstract: WikiTrace links each agent-memory lesson to its source trajectory so an agent can inspect missing details, conflicts, or failed-task evidence before acting; the authors report consistent gains over memory baselines on five agentic benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors store concise insights with summaries and links to raw trajectories, then use tools to inspect the linked evidence when a lesson lacks detail, conflicts with another, or derives from a failed task.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say trajectory diagnoses may be wrong and links do not themselves verify insights; placing every insight in the initial prompt also makes prompt size grow, leaving retrieval for oversized memories open.

sections.title: Margin-Guided Token Credit for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
sections.abstract: MCPO redistributes sequence-level reinforcement-learning credit toward tokens with a small top-two probability margin, reporting gains over GRPO on two small language models while generating longer answers.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors use the trainer’s existing forward pass to read top-two token margins and redistribute advantages; they report a 6.55-point mean macro avg@32 gain over GRPO for MiniCPM5-2B-Base and a positive three-seed Qwen3-4B-Base replication.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors did not compare against entropy-based credit or a length-matched baseline, so they cannot separate the margin-credit effect from the observed increase in answer length; the comparison uses one short LoRA training recipe.
